utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. The situation continues from yesterday as regards Judge Morrison, so we will continue to sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Could we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber notes the request filed today by the Prosecution for leave to file a reply to the accused's response to Prosecution's second motion to admit evidence of Slobodan Stojkovic without cross-examination, filed on the 21st of February, 2012. The Chamber considers that it would be of assistance to the Chamber in deciding on the issue and therefore grants this request. Unless there are any other matters, then we'll bring in the witness. In the meantime, we'll give the exhibit number for the public redacted version for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P4100, 4100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before we move forward, I would just like to deal with a couple of things from yesterday while it might be fresher in yours and everyone's mind, and to begin with I'd like to go back to the organigramme we talked about yesterday. That's now got the Exhibit number P4446, and I think you still have a copy of that organigramme on the table in front of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your explanation in the Tolimir case about the structures of the Main Staff and their relationships to one another, you explained the concept of professional control over some units that we see here depicted on the organigramme, saying that professional control does not entail the power to issue orders. The line of issuing orders goes along the line of subordination, which means from the commander. And that's at pages 11960 to 11962. Do you remember giving that explanation, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, then on the subject of this professional control, I'd like to go back to this organigramme for a little while and have you talk about a couple of the units that we didn't spend much time with yesterday. First, I'd like to draw your attention to a unit depicted on the bottom left-hand corner, the 67th Communications Regiment. Now, in the Tolimir -- in your Tolimir testimony, you said of this regiment: "Its main task is to organise the communications, to satisfy the communications needs of the Main Staff. It's attached to the commander. In performing its professional duties, it's attached to the arms within the staff sector." That was at pages 11960 to 11961. So when you say this unit is attached to the commander specifically, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line of subordination I explained in general terms. It goes down from the commander to the various sectors, the independent administrations, and all the units that you have lined up at the bottom. With regard to the 67th Communications Regiment, the chain of command, as they say in Croatia, or the line of subordination is the black one. It goes down from the commander and then to all the other levels. When Tolimir was contacted about that equipment if that's the case you're referring to in the staff sector, there's a chief of communications of that branch, and he is a professional organ. And through operational evidence, he monitors the condition in the 67th Communications Regiment with regard to his communications equipment, with regard to the staff, the manpower, and he is responsible for their professional training. If at one point in time General Miletic played the role of coordinator in the staff sector instead of General Milovanovic, well, in that case it was his responsibility to contact the chief of communications and assign him the task that General Tolimir had requested to be carried out, the task that has to do with those encryption devices and the K/2 device.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you've just indicated that the line of subordination from the commander to the 67th Communications Unit is the black one. Now, does this dotted line to the staff sector --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the commander to the Communications Regiment, it's the black line, and as for the professional organ, it's the red line. The dotted red line that links up with the 67th Communications Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go over to the other side of the organigramme --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. That dotted red line should be connected to chief of communication? Is it your evidence, General Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is connected to the staff sector, but within the staff sector, the communications organ is part of the organ for the arms -- the arms and services and they're subordinated to the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So having heard that with respect to the 67th Communications Regiment, maybe we could move over to something called the 10th Sabotage Detachment which is on the right-hand side of the organigramme at the bottom. And in your Tolimir testimony at page 11960, you said similarly: "This unit was under the command of the commander while, professionally speaking, they were in a certain sense subordinated to the intelligence administration because of their reconnaissance tasks." Could you explain then in the case of this unit what you mean by professional subordination?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as in the case of these organs of the arms and services in the staff sector, every has its own field of operations. An infantryman is concerned with the infantry equipment, the staff. He must tell the Chief of Staff if asked what sort of equipment he has. He must provide him with that information. Similarly, the chief of an armed mechanised unit, well, they are responsible for training their units, for keeping records, and this is all done independently. In the case of anti-aircraft defence, the chief of the anti-aircraft defence, he has to act in a similar manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us clarify, because the terms you are using are not consistent with the words that appear in the organigramme, so we are a bit confused. You said chief of armed mechanised unit. Did you mean chief of artillery or chief of armoured and mechanised units? Did you refer to Colonel Trkulja?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Armoured and mechanised units. Colonel Trkulja was the chief of those units. The chief of engineering, the chief of intelligence, all these chiefs are responsible for their fields, for their profession. They have to keep professional records. They have to monitor the equipment situation, the training of the men. They must always be able to submit suggestions to the chief of the staff and he has to submit suggestions to the commander. So the chief of the intelligence administration, Colonel Salapura, for example, in professional terms he keeps operational records for reconnaissance purposes, for training the men. He has such activities for the Sabotage Detachment. So that is the professional aspect of their responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was Colonel Salapura in the position to give orders directly to the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He could have if the commander had authorised him to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So then, General, do you think the red dotted line on this organigramme linking the 10th Sabotage Detachment to Colonel Salapura accurately reflects - pardon me - this unit's professional subordination that you've just been describing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just who would be responsible then for Colonel Salapura and his professional control of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first superior of Colonel Salapura was General Tolimir as the chief of sector for intelligence and security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Similarly, was General Tolimir in a position to give orders directly to the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like Salapura, with the authorisation from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And then finally if we could go over back to the left side of the organigramme, we have something, a unit called the 65th Protection Regiment. Who was its commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milomir Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, also in your Tolimir testimony at page 11962, you indicated that when it's about issuing orders, this unit was related to the commander, and you also pointed out that this unit contained a battalion of military police and that -- and you said that the security administration contained a department in charge of military police affairs. So then what I'd like to know is did the security administration have professional control over the work of the military police battalion of this unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intelligence or security? What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I specifically said security administration.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the professional line, yes, and through the detachment for the work of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the nature of that professional control? Could you give us an idea what you mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They monitor work in professional terms. It only concerns these police tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In professional terms meaning in what way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this department, the people who completed certain security courses and they were intended for the work of the organs of the military police. These people exercise control in professional terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who heads the security administration?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who is he responsible to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the chief of sector for intelligence and security affairs, to General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is Colonel Beara in a position to give orders to the military police battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On condition that he received such authorisation from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And would that be the same case with his superior who on this organigramme is listed as General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So does the dotted line linking the military police battalion of this 65th Protection Regiment to the security administration accurately depict the relationship you've just described?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If in respect of this organigramme Your Honours have no other questions at this time, I would move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one question. That dotted line from the security administration, i.e., the professional line, is connected to military police battalion, not to the 65th Protection Regiment. Am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the military police unit. From the regiment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Colonel Beara does not exercise professional control over Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, performing such duties would be done through the regiment commander. I don't know why this was separated here. It should be related to the regiment. The commander of the regiment cannot be bypassed. This military police battalion should not have been indicated separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll still move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General Obradovic, yesterday I asked you whether the commander or other members of the Main Staff had meetings with Dr. Karadzic, and after I reminded you of a question and answer during your evidence in the Popovic case, you said those meetings were within the context of an analysis of combat readiness, and when such analysis were discussed, then there would be political representatives attending. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the case, because what you have just referred to was four years ago. I think the question concerned General Milovanovic in particular, and the lawyer Petrusic asked whether Miletic was replacing and I said yes. General Milovanovic went to govern meetings and meetings of the Assembly, I believe. So that was the question. And yesterday I thought the question concerned the analysis of combat readiness. Yes. They went to meetings with the supreme commander, but as to how frequently and so on and so forth, I don't know, but there were contacts. They went to government meetings when military issues were also discussed. In 1996, on one occasion, I also went at the beginning of July, I think, to a government meeting where the agenda concerned the military. There were four or five of us and we were led by the Chief of Staff. And that item was item number 18. They put it right at the top. So this was the first item that was discussed so that they could let us go.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, General, about this analysis of combat readiness you mentioned yesterday. Who takes part all together in this combat readiness analysis?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire army takes part in the analysis of combat readiness. How do they do this? Well, an analysis is performed for the previous year. This is completed in battalions and divisions. They then refer the case to the commands of brigades and regiments. The commands of brigades and regiments refer the case to the corps command. They then perform analysis of combat readiness there. And when the analysis are completed at the level of the corps command, the level of anti-aircraft defence and in military academies, then you have a combat analysis at the level of the Main Staff, at the level the army. And these annual analysis of combat readiness is an analysis that the political organs participate in. They were in a certain sense present.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was there -- at the level of the Main Staff, was there an analysis, as you've just described, done in 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, it was at the end of January that this analysis was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And did the political organs take part in that analysis in 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: When you refer to the political organs, who do you mean in particular?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the president, the vice-presidents, the minister of defence, the speaker of parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: When you speak of the analysis at the Main Staff level, are there any conclusions drawn as a result?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of a plan that is made and when lower-ranking units are informed as to the time and place, then this plan says specifically commander starts the analysis. This goes on for five or ten minutes, and then the 1st Corps follows and the 2nd Corps and so on and so forth, and then the commanders of other units and representatives of military schools and then the chiefs of sectors and of these two independent administrations. The corps commanders, when they take part in the discussion, they finish their remarks by making certain proposals regarding the following period, and then on the basis of that, tasks should be formulated and incorporated into directives as combat documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just relating to the answer you've just given, how does the president take part in these presentations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He listens to the presentations of the commanders of subordinate units and representatives of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does the president take part? Does he speak?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't present. I don't know whether he took the floor or not, but objectively speaking, he would address the gathering.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You mentioned that this -- this analysis would result in tasks which are formulated and incorporated into directives as combat documents. Now, you spoke at length during your testimony in the Tolimir case about directives, and I'm wondering whether the conclusions from this analysis have any relationship with the directives you discussed in your Tolimir testimony.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, part of the tasks and obligations that are formulated as tasks for the forthcoming period are defined as tasks in the directive as a general combat document. So these are the tasks issued to the subordinates. Directives are combat documents of high commands that spell out for the future, for a longer period, important conclusions relating to combat activities. Detailed tasks are not given to units in these documents. It is the objectives of the activities that are spelled out, the general task and the basic idea of the commander. So subordinate commanders receive through these documents the necessary elements for their own independent planning and execution of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did the analysis of combat readiness which you've just spoken about that was conducted in 1995 have any relationship with directive 7?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to have the documents now and if we would look at conclusions and tasks for particular corps, we would probably see what was proposed to corps commanders, and we would probably see certain tasks that were part of the directive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that we have to intervene in the transcript where it says that this was proposed to corps, but he said what the corps proposed. If I understood this correctly, during the analysis, corps present what the situation was in relation to combat readiness, and they present their proposals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm, General Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said what the corps commanders proposed was included to a large extent in the directive.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you mean to say what the corps commanders proposed during the course of this analysis of combat readiness we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They presented proposals regarding tasks. They made these proposals to the command of the Main Staff and the Supreme Command for the forthcoming period.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. Just a point of clarification -- just a point of clarification from yesterday. You said at page 25095 that all these reports from the corps, from the anti-aircraft, from the schools, and so on, came to the Main Staff, to the staff sector, to the administration for operations and training. And His Honour Judge Kwon asked: "I take it that that organ, or that unit, receives all the reports addressed to the Main Staff." And you answered, "Yes." And as I said, by way of clarification, did your answer refer to reports from all the military sectors or only to operations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It referred to daily operations reports from subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did the other Main Staff sectors similarly receive supports in their areas of responsibility from subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in the professional field. So this had to do with command, whereas this meant that logistics organs received through their own organs daily reports, and they followed the amounts of materiel that were being used, ammunition, fuel, food, and so on, whereas the chiefs of the arms and services were reported to on these professional tasks that pertained to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So then in addition to the operational reports we discussed yesterday, do you know whether the president received reports from other sectors?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we'll go back to the series of documents we were dealing with when we broke yesterday - pardon me - which were related to convoy movement. The first one I'd like to deal with is P4189, please. It's a communication dated 31 March 1993, to UNPROFOR command, signed on behalf of General Milovanovic, and listing a series of 14 convoys which were not approved for movement across VRS-held territory. Now, General, you recall looking at this document in preparation for your testimony here today, I suspect, don't you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So this is a document of several pages, and my questions about this are rather brief. Could you first of all have a look at the bottom of the first page and tell us whether you recognise the signature of who signed on behalf of General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the signature of General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could we go over to page 2 of both documents, and briefly, the successive pages, and my question is, General, if you could look at this first page and -- or this second page, it is. Could you tell us whether you recognise those handwritten initials that appear at the top of the page beside the circled word "Ne" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the initials of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I wonder if my colleague could now flip to the next page in succession, and I would simply like the general to look at similar notations at the top of each page of this document. So, General --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Whose initials are these, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same of the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And do you remember looking through this document and recognising the same initials at the top of every page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we show him page 9 then. You'll come to that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Same question, General, with respect to this next page. Whose initials are those?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I recognise them. The initials are those of the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the next page.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same here.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: On -- is every page of this -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Page 7, the same --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Page 8 next, please. Whose initials are these, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same. The same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And page 9.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, the notations here, though, General, have one small change. There seems to be a "yes" initially written and, I think the word underneath it might read something like "limit," if I'm not mistaken, although it's not translated in the English version. Do you see that difference?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Yes," and then "through," and then in Cyrillic it says "limit," or "restriction," and then that is crossed out. And then it says "no," and then the commander initialed that. He probably had given his approval in a limited way, but what affected his decision to make the definite answer no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So is "Da" also handwriting of Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. This has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It has indeed. Could we go next to P839.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's a communication dated 7 April 1995 from the Main Staff to the Drina Corps command with the signature block of General Milovanovic informing that the Main Staff concurs with the implementation of permits from the co-ordinating body for humanitarian assistance to Republika Srpska but listing items from those convoys that weren't approved. General, if we could scroll down a little bit in the B/C/S version, do you see a remark towards the bottom of page 1 that says that material for the Swedish construction project for Srebrenica will not be approved until the Main Staff receives the position of the State Committee for Cooperation on this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I just asked if you saw the paragraph that I had just about read out to you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is this the same State Committee for Cooperation headed by Dr. Koljevic you referred to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it pertains to the same one.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does this letter reflect co-ordination between the VRS civil affairs administration and the political organ?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Where do you see co-operation? This one sentence in this one paragraph that you're referring to, and it has to do with the material for the Swedish construction project for Srebrenica and in Drinjaca on the 9th of April, 11th of April, and 13th of April, 1995, for Srebrenica, full stop. Until we receive the position of the state committee regarding this matter. They probably did not receive anything from the state committee, and they probably could not give their consent until the committee stated its position. The fax could have reached the department apart from the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go now to 65 ter number 03640, dated 14 April 1995. It's a communication from the VRS Main Staff to military post 7111, notifying them of the approval and refusal of a number of convoys, signed by General Miletic. My first question, General, is: Where was military post 7111?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I don't know. But judging by this stamp up here where it says 7119, it pertains to some Zvornik Brigade. Possibly the Drina Corps was military post 7111.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go over on the next page to items 12 and 13 of this document in B/C/S, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, could you just have a look at those two items, 12 and 13, which refuse the passage of convoys to Gorazde and Zepa, relieving UN military observers and translators. And my question in relation to those two items is: Would you be able to explain for us what concerns the VRS Main Staff might have in terms of relieving UN military observers and translators in those areas?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what led the commander to make this kind of decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The last sentence of this communication tells the recipients to inform check-points of the above and in case one of the convoys or individual vehicles appears act as ordered. Whose orders would General Miletic have been referring to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the commander's orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be a Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Given that the -- the limited amount of information the witness gave about this document, I'm wondering if we could just pass it for the moment and I can discuss it with Dr. Karadzic whether or not we want to object to this particular document. I know there are documents we also want to use with respect to convoys and it may not be in our interest to object, but on the other hand, listening to the answers, it didn't seem like the witness really confirmed anything about the document, particularly the fact that he was not -- he was on leave during this period in addition. But if you would just leave it as it is right now and we can come back to it at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like you to come back after the break. Yes. Let's move on, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter number 03700.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's a document dated 2 June 1995, to the command of military posts 7111 and 7102, signed by General Miletic, indicating they agree with the approval of the co-ordinating body for HRRS for a number of convoys but refusing from those the transport of school supplies, oil for saws, and something called the Swedish construction project for Srebrenica. So my question, General, about this document is what -- in order for this document to issue, would this have gone through the same process you described in your evidence yesterday, the process of approval following review?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see, General, any military justification for the Main Staff refusing - pardon me - the transport of one truck of school supplies to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot go into the reasons, especially in view of the fact that I wasn't there. And even if I had been there, I don't know what a particular person or commander is guided by in a restrictive approach.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: On the -- on the face of the document, do you see any military justification for refusing the transport of school supplies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: School supplies? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be a Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should we do the same with respect to this? Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The reason you are putting these questions, i.e., the convoy matters, to this witness is to strengthen your case given the next witness can deal with this more appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Obradovic was within the Main Staff. He's spoken about the administration and able to identify the department from which these documents emanate. He's talked about the process through which these documents would have gone before they're issued. So actually, Your Honour, I think even though he might not have been able to answer with respect to the last document my question relating to the content, his comments are more than sufficient to allow for the document's admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. Could you explore with him whether he can answer my question that I put to Mr. Momir Nikolic, i.e., whether there were separate rules for the humanitarian convoy on the one hand, and the military convoy on the other hand? I think general mentioned briefly yesterday, but if you could clarify with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, are you aware as to whether there were separate rules regarding the passage of humanitarian convoys as opposed to military convoys in effect -- pardon me, convoys across VRS territory?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were. When it came to supply convoys for the peacekeeping forces, it frequently happened that, for example, they asked to be replenished with ammunition in the enclave without carrying out any training or shooting exercise, and the question was where was that ammunition then spent? So, for example, they also applied for large quantities of fuel for their resources in the enclave, and in our view it was far beyond their realistic needs. It all made us suspect that the fuel in question may end up in enemy hands. That was the difference between military and humanitarian supply convoys. The state committee held a wider jurisdiction in terms of humanitarian convoys, and the army held the authority with regard to UNPROFOR convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But, General, what we see in these documents, this one in particular, implies an overlap of authority between these two organs, if I can call them that, because in the document before us, we see what appears to be the military authorities imposing a restriction on convoys approved by political organs.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely what guided the person who made the decision, but he had the responsibility for the situation in the field, and obviously the person in question had problems with such military issues or supplies. The standing committee as a political body established by the civilian authorities probably dealt less with such military matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, did they work in conjunction with one another?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably did, because in the preamble they are both referred to. In other words, they were in contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could I intervene, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us check whether my understanding is correct, General Obradovic. Let's start with this purely military convoy or UNPROFOR convoy. The state committee had nothing to do with such military convoy. Such convoys would be dealt with exclusively by the VRS. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In case of the humanitarian convoys, UNHCR, ICRC, or various organs, they were initially dealt with by the state committee. However, even if the state committee gave consent to such convoys, VRS had discretion on -- on the basis of military reasons not to agree with some decisions of the state committee. That's why we see the formulation "We agree with the approval" in such documents as this. Am I correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because the army was responsible for the situation in the field. Humanitarian convoys, too, had some sort of escort, military escort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An intervention in the transcript. Line 5, page 23. The witness said they were probably in contact, whereas we don't have the word "probably."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, let's continue, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to go next to 65 ter number 03703, dated 12 June 1995, from the VRS Main Staff signed by General Miletic to the Drina Corps. Now, this document also relates to convoys, agreeing with authorisations issued by the organ called the HRRS, and it pertains to members of Medecins sans Frontieres leaving Srebrenica, but this document has a remark --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we just -- I think the General might not be able to see the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This document has a remark noting, among other things, that no foreign MSF officials shall be allowed to enter the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you remove the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at the document now, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, is this consistent with the answer that you've just given Judge Kwon to the effect that the military -- the department for -- the VRS department for civil affairs had discretion not to agree with decisions of the state committee?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a remark in the document which states: "In the request submitted, there is information about personnel shifts or rotations, which is not allowed." I am not familiar with the context of it all. The next sentence says: "Only the specified persons have been approved to leave the enclave. Igor Mindiouk from Srebrenica," and someone else from Gorazde. I don't know where they belonged.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, this document also in the last sentence reads: "In other words, no foreign Medecins sans Frontieres officials will be allowed to enter the enclaves except perhaps for some drivers." So I'm wondering, General, if this conditional approval is consistent with the situation you've just explained to Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It seems that the two people in question were allowed to leave Srebrenica and Gorazde. The person who is to implement this document at the check-point is reminded that no foreigners are allowed to enter the enclave save for the drivers who may appear at the check-point with the aim of transporting these two people out.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, do you have any idea what interest the VRS Main Staff would have had in preventing Medecins sans Frontieres from entering the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the abbreviation MSF stands for.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I thought I had just said Medecins sans Frontieres. Doctors Without Borders.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the person making the decision was guided by.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be marked as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with it at one go after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll move on. 65 ter number 03546, please. It's a document from the VRS Main Staff, dated 3 July 1995, to the Drina Corps command, approving a DutchBat convoy of 20 men leaving Srebrenica but not approving the convoy's return. I'm sorry, but is there any way you can just shift the B/C/S version a little bit over to the right so the General can see all of the text? He misses just a little bit. Or to the left then.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, what effect does this refusal for return of the convoy have on UNPROFOR's manpower levels in Srebrenica at this time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why this decision was made that no return be allowed. It seems logical that if some people left and others did not go in they will be short of personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And for the last convoy-related document, can we see 65 ter number 03548. I think it might have a suffix A, small A. It's a document from the VRS Main Staff dated 5 July 1995, to military posts 7598 and 7111, signed by General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: There's no suffix A on it apparently. It's 03548.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, paragraph 4 of this document refers to the approved medical evacuation from Srebrenica of a Dutch soldier, specifically instructing that this convoy should be exhaustively checked at the Yellow Bridge to prevent photo and video material being taken out, and that if you find any such material, it is to be confiscated and the Main Staff is to be informed. Is this a convoy request, General, that would have fallen strictly within the area of responsibility of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Can you see paragraph 4? Probably page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And now on the English version we have to go over to the next page for paragraph 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, is this a document that would have fallen strictly within the area of responsibility of the VRS civil affairs office in terms of its processing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have in mind the restriction pertaining to video and photographic material, it was rather a security matter. It was more that than the area of responsibility of the department that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So then in terms of the processing of this request, who would have been involved in the review?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything specific. I was not present when the document was created. However, if for some reasons, counter-intelligence reasons, such information may have arrived from the security administration or from intelligence administration in order to protect military information and the positions of the VRS that may have been located along the route of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, what interest would the Main Staff have in preventing photo and video material being taken out of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what made the security or intelligence organ decide this.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move on to another topic now and talk about some of the daily operations reports to the president that we were discussing yesterday and look at some examples of the type of information contained in those reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter number 04116.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And while we wait, perhaps I could ask you, General, among other things, did the operations reports that were sent to Dr. Karadzic include such things as information on the military's engagement in active combat or the implementation of operational plans?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have discussed the contents of daily operations reports yesterday. They contained information about the enemy, possible intentions and situation. It also contained information about our own forces in terms of grouping intentions and tasks, as well as losses in materiel and personnel. It also had information about adjacent units and any new corps commanders' decisions if there were any that were needed to continue with the activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we just go over to the very last page of this document which was issued by General Miletic on behalf of the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, above the signature block do you see the initials "nt/pm"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you know who those refer to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These maybe the initials of the Nedeljko Trkulja. And then after the slash it may have been Paulina Mitrovic, a stenographer or typist.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Who was Nedeljko Trkulja?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Nedeljko Trkulja was in the Main Staff, in the staff sector of the Main Staff. He was head of -- or chief of armoured mechanised units organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we go over to paragraph 6 on B/C/S page 3. And I'll just wait until paragraph 6 in English comes up.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, paragraph 6(b) reads that the main body of the force is engaged in persistent defence -- pardon me. Paragraph 6(b) which refers to events in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps reads that: "The main body of the force is engaged in persistent defence while a part of the forces is engaged in active combat operations, especially around the Srebrenica enclave where they are carrying out combat tasks as planned." Is this an example of reports to Dr. Karadzic which talk about the implementation of operational plans?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be a Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P4449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we now go to 65 ter number 03969, which is a VRS Main Staff operations report to the president on 11 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, as you've indicated, these operations reports could also include information on significant territorial gains or military developments. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go over, please, to paragraph 6(b) again on B/C/S page 3, relating to the situation in the Drina Corps zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And there in paragraph 6(b), it reads that: "In the course of the day, our forces entered the town of Srebrenica." Is this an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is this an example of one of those reports that includes information on significant territorial gains or military developments?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure where the sentence you quoted is precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Paragraph 6(b).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the witness could read out the entire paragraph, as well as the date when it was received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you find the paragraph, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6(b)? "The situation in the corps. The corps units are at full combat readiness. The main body of the forces is engaged in persistent defence while parts of the forces are engaged in offensive operations around the enclave of Srebrenica. During the day our forces entered the town of Srebrenica. Regarding the results achieved and other details" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document. Could that be a Prosecution exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We don't have any objection to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted as Exhibit P4450. Shall we take a break if it is convenient with you, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will break for half an hour and resume at 3.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon again. The proceedings have been delayed due to technical difficulties, and for the same reason, we will sit here at Courtroom III tomorrow as well. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We do not have any objection to the admission of the exhibits that we discussed before the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for your reminder. I think we have -- we dealt with five documents, Ms. Edgerton, 65 ter number 3640, 3700, 3703, 3546, 3548. They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P4451 through P4455 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Edgerton, how long do you have, just for planning purposes?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll try and keep it to around 45 minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, you confirmed in your Tolimir testimony that information from the VRS corps level operations report was put into or inserted into the VRS Main Staff reports to the president; is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's page 11982 in the transcript of the Tolimir testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Pardon me. I'd like to then look at a corps-level report, 65 ter number 02004, from the Drina Corps command to the VRS Main Staff, dated 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, just a couple of questions about this document, General. If you look at the reference number on the top left-hand side above the date, you'll see that it begins with 03. Does that number indicate anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 03 indicates the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does it indicate any sector of the staff in particular?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 03/4 refers to the administration for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Just going back for a moment to this page 11982 that we were given the reference for, it was -- if you look at the transcript, actually, he was speaking of a --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give me a minute. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. He was actually asked a question about a specific document with respect to Zepa, and his answer was, "Yes. That was taken over from a Drina Corps report." And I believe in other parts of his testimony he indicated that the reports that went to the president were reduced from the -- by the information that was reported by the Drina Corps to the Main Staff, and so I don't think that the question -- that the reference given by Ms. Edgerton actually fairly reflects her question, so I -- it's often Dr. Karadzic who is the one who is being questioned about his references, and I think that it's only fair that when a reference by the Prosecutor is not quite right that we point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And is this -- if we could turn over to the very last page of this document and then I'll have another question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, having seen both pages of this report, is this operations report from the Drina Corps something that would have been received within your sector at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, a minute ago I was asked about this number on the first page. I thought it was a report from the Main Staff to the commander, and I said it was 03/4, but it's a Drina Corps report, so I couldn't really say which organ is concerned, but obviously the reports are from the Drina Corps. Here it says: "For the commander." I don't know who signed it, but given the contents of the report, the contents as such would be forwarded in accordance with the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So was this something that would have been received within your sector in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please go back to the first page so that I can see how it has been laid out. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I heard you --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, here in this document do you see the second sort of subparagraph under section 2, under the heading "Combat readiness," which reads: "The terrain is being combed in the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion zone of responsibility, and a large number of Muslims fleeing from the Srebrenica enclave have been surrendering." Are you able to identify that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This concerns the Independent Skelani Infantry Battalion. It says that the terrain is being combed, and a large number of Muslims fleeing from the Srebrenica enclave have been surrendering.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now could we go to 65 ter number 01918. It's a VRS Main Staff report to the president on the same date, 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, did you mean to tender that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not at this moment. I'd like to deal with the next document and then move both of them in, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, do you see this Main Staff report to the president and the corps of the army on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, this number that appears just above the date on the top left-hand corner of the page, 03/3-195, what does that denote?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administration for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's -- is that the sector that you served in?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the administration that is within the staff sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And is this then the administration that issued this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since it's been registered, recorded, I assume that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we now please go over to paragraph 6(b), which relates to the situation in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. That's B/C/S page 3 and English page 3 as well, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, under heading 6(b), General, do you see where it reads: "The main body of the corps is engaged in defence whereas the Milici and Bratunac brigades as well as the Skelani Independent Battalion are scouring the terrain and receiving a large number of Muslim fugitives who are surrendering to them"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, is this information very similar to the information we just saw laid out in the Drina Corps command report?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And do you know how that would come about? Why is the information so very similar?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of reporting is to provide accurate information on the events in the field. The information provided should not diverge in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Diverge in any way from what?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, diverge from the information contained in the Drina Corps report.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was -- are you describing a practice, then, in the method of compiling or preparing the reports to the president?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't have to be identical. It's not necessary to copy the contents of a given report, but the essence of the events has to be accurately conveyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we, just before we leave this document, go to the very last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see just above the signature block, which reads "General Miletic standing in for the Chief of Staff," the initials "nt/gp"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Whose initials are those, do you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume those are the initials of Nedeljko Trkulja from the staff sector, but I don't know who the typist is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to move both of those documents now in as Prosecution exhibits, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Both will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P4456 and P4457 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we now see another Drina Corps report to the VRS Main Staff, 65 ter number 02018, dated 18 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see the report I've just mentioned on the screen in front of you, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And does this report come from the same sector as the previous Drina Corps report we've just looked at?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I look at the number, I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we go over to the last page of the document in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And do you see whose signature block appears on this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the name that's been printed, but I don't know whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Whose's name's been printed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Major-General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who was he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, could we just move over -- back over to heading 1 of this document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, at the beginning, I think it's the first, second, third, fourth line down from the top of heading 1, you see the report that begins: "Parts of broken forces from Srebrenica organised into smaller formations continued their attempts to break through the brigade's zone towards Tuzla. In the general Planinica and Potocani sector, small groups were discovered and mostly destroyed, but a small number got through our position during the night of 17/18 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we now go to the VRS Main Staff report to the president, also dated 18 July, 65 ter number 4009.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the sake of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, once again, this document, the line above the date bears the number 03/3-199. Does that number denote anything?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that this is a number used for the operations and training administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your administration, in other words.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we please go over to section 6 of this document in both languages, and it's on the fourth page in B/C/S and I think the sixth page in English. Oh, I've got my numbers wrong in B/C/S. Your indulgence for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You mean 6(b).

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page for the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, about halfway through this paragraph 6(a), and I'll just try and identify the line for you, your indulgence for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you mean the last sentence: "Blocking and destroying the broken up Muslim formations"?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I actually see it halfway through the top paragraph on the English page and I think it's the one, two, three, four, five, sixth sentence from the top of paragraph 6(a).

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: After mention of the name Sopotnica-Kopaci, do you see reference to: "The broken-up enemy forces from the Srebrenica enclave have been trying to break through towards Tuzla in smaller groups"? Do you see that line, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Here again this language is very similar from the report generated by the Drina Corps. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's similar, but there are other elements that concern a unit that appeared and that was withdrawing in the direction of Udrc.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: How would your sector ensure consistency in the information? Was there a methodology applied in preparing the reports that went to the president?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no methodology. The methodology was quite clear. On the basis of subordinate reports, one would draft reports that would be forwarded to one's superiors.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have these two, 65 ter number 02018 and 04009, as Prosecution exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibits P4458 and P4459 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we go now to a VRS Main Staff report to the president dated 15 July 1995, 65 ter number 01919.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see that report on the screen in front of you, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is this report, like the previous reports, generated by your administration?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from the staff sector. It's not mine, but, yes, the number is the number used for the operations and training administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we please go over to the very last page, signature-block page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, here we have initials "nt/mm" just above the signature block. Do you know -- pardon me. Does "nt," to your knowledge, refer to the same "nt" in the previous documents, Nedeljko Trkulja?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume it refers to the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could go over to paragraph 6(b), which is on English pages 3 and 4, and I think the bottom of B/C/S page 3, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Under the heading "Situation in the corps," which is at the bottom of the page you see in front of you, it reports: "The 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade with its reinforcements is carrying out preparations to cut off and encircle enemy soldiers en route from Planinica to Kljevci. The 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion have used some of their troops to scour the terrain in order to discover the enemy groups which are lagging behind." Would this information have been drawn from, based on your experience, reports originating from the Drina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be a Prosecution exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4460, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: One more VRS Main Staff report to the president, please, dated 19 July 1995. It's 65 ter number 13606.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Once again, General, we see a document with the same prefix to the reference number 03, and does this then indicate that it was issued by the same department as the previous Main Staff operations reports we've been viewing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And once again, can we just go over to the signature block on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: There's different initials here that appear above the signature block which is General Miletic's signature block. Do you -- can you tell us who those initials might represent?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to be "sb."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who was named "sb" within the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of initials and in terms of the first and last name, it could be Bogdan Sladojevic. Now, whether it is him or not, I cannot say. I don't know if there's anybody else with these initials "sb."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we go over to paragraph 6(a) under the heading "Zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps," and 6(a) is the sub-heading "Enemy." In English you have to go just one page further to get the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 6(a) under the heading "Enemy," we see the report that: "In the zone of the responsibility of the 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, enemy formations from the Srebrenica enclave were smashed and surrounded in Planinci and Baljkovici villages, and in sectors Bijela Zemlja and Gornja Kamenica, enemy groups are attempting to break through to Muslim-controlled territory. On the front facing Gorazde, the enemy attacked the Sjenokos and the Jabucko Sedlo features with infantry weapons." Now, as was the case with the previous reports to the president, is this information that would have been drawn from the operations reports received in the Main Staff from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could that be a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4461, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, General, this document was dated 18 July, and I'm just wondering if that's before or after the date that you returned to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, was it not 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It was indeed. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was that before or after you returned to active service in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And when did you return?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And where did you come from to return to Main Staff headquarters?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And where did you spend your sick leave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And how did you travel from Derventa to Main Staff headquarters?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By car. Somebody else drove me. It wasn't my car.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what route did you take?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijeljina, Zvornik, Drinjaca, Milici, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you en route receive any information related to the security situation during your travels?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we were warned in Zvornik that there were some armed groups that were crossing that road and that we should be careful because there were cases of action taken against cars. People were killed, wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you receive any information as to where those armed groups had come from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, when you got back to Main Staff headquarters, did you resume your previous duties?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As usual, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And as part of those duties, did you continue to receive and review operations reports from the corps on the situation in the field?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we compiled a list because the operations centre had never really started operating. Then we compiled a list. People who were free, who were not involved somewhere in the field, they would write the report for that day. They would take the report and write it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: When you say "write it up," are you referring -- what -- what would you be writing up? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the daily operations report to the supreme commander and subordinate units and also forward command posts that were active at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In order to write up that report, did you receive or review reports, corps-level operations reports?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to me personally?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Given the answer to your previous question, yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not I personally. It was the person who compiled the report, the person who was assigned to write that report on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you receive or did you become aware of the situation in the theatre as a consequence of your duties following your return?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I knew on the whole what was going on, that an attack had been carried out against the enclave, that the forces from the enclave had been crushed. I heard about that as I was travelling since they had told me to be careful when covering that part of the route.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have a look, please, at 65 ter number 136 -- pardon me. 65 ter number 02058. It's a document dated 25 July 1995, from the 1st Podrinje Brigade, signed by General Tolimir, entitled "Agreement on the disarmament of Zepa."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the previous trials. Now, was it 2008 or Tolimir, but anyway, I don't know. I did see them, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, paragraph 4 of this document in B/C/S, which I think is actually at the bottom of this page. My mistake. It's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should refer to the English portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's my problem with numbers. I have a degree in English, not mathematics, Your Honour. If we could please scroll up in both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 1 in English?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. It's the one -- first, second, third paragraph from the top, which reads: "Our commission should demand all our war prisoners, including ones from Gorazde and Bihac. Our war prisoners have to be released between 25 and 28 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, General, as you were familiar with the situation at the time, I wonder if you could explain to us effectively what's the rush? Why do all Serb prisoners have to be released over this three-day period that starts with the very same date of this letter, 25 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
